Supporting Canoe Valley School

Canoe Valley School is a community-supported project, and financial gifts are essential to bringing the school into being. Canoe Valley School is a registered 501(c)(3) tax-exempt Iowa non-profit corporation.

Donate online Give by check

Trouble with the form? Donate on Give Lively’s site instead.

Phase 1 fundraising goals

$300,000

Our Phase 1 goal is to raise $300,000 to prepare Canoe Valley School for its first students.

$50,000
To establish the school through organizational development, program planning, early staffing, curriculum work, accreditation preparation, communications, and launch-year readiness.
$250,000
To support renovations and site work, including the ground-floor classrooms, accessibility improvements, basic infrastructure, and other initial improvements toward a campus that can support the school’s full vision.

A seed for growth

Phase 1 of our campus development will focus on renovating the ground floor of the existing building to create two functional classrooms for Canoe Valley’s first students.

These spaces will allow the school to launch its initial cohort within the current structure while larger campus improvements continue over time. In addition to the two classrooms, the project will include infrastructure upgrades, restroom modernization, and other necessary improvements to meet modern safety requirements for a school building.

Your gift helps create a place where adolescents can learn through meaningful projects, mentorship, practical work, ecological connection, and service to the wider community.

Designated gifts and questions

Where your gift can go

Phase 1 Capital Fund
Supports Phase 1 renovations, including renovation of classrooms and shared learning spaces.
School Launch Donation
Supports initial school setup, curriculum development, and equipment.
Scholarships
Supports need-based assistance to students attending Canoe Valley School.
Endowment
Supports expansion and long-term sustainability of the school’s offerings, including long-term scholarship funds, and funds to support operations and capital improvements over time.
Planned Giving
Supports the school’s long-term financial health through thoughtful estate planning coordination.

Gifts toward the campus plan

We also welcome gifts directed toward specific elements of the master plan. Whether supporting the full Phase 1 goal or giving toward a particular campus element, each donation helps bring Canoe Valley School from vision into daily life.

Community Room
A flexible gathering space for showcases, performances, meetings, meals, exhibitions, and community events.
Gazebo
A sheltered outdoor classroom and gathering place that supports learning in all seasons.
Learning Barn
A future anchor for farm-based learning, practical work, animal care, storage, and hands-on projects.
Play Area
A natural space for movement, exploration, imagination, and intergenerational community use.
Amphitheater
An outdoor setting for presentations, performances, councils, storytelling, and seasonal gatherings.
Gardens and Orchard
Living classrooms for ecological arts, regenerative growing, food systems, and place-based learning.

Other ways to support us

Canoe Valley School will grow through the care, imagination, labor, and generosity of families, neighbors, educators, mentors, and local partners who believe young people need meaningful places to learn, belong, and contribute. There are many ways to help:

  • Volunteer on a school committee to support planning in areas like curriculum, facilities, governance, fundraising, communications, or community partnerships.
  • Become a mentor by sharing your craft, profession, land-based knowledge, artistic practice, technical skill, or life experience with students.
  • Offer in-kind labor or materials to help renovate the building, improve outdoor learning spaces, support farm and garden infrastructure, or equip classrooms and studios.
  • Contribute professional services such as legal, financial, design, construction, communications, grant-writing, nonprofit, or educational expertise.
  • Host or support community events that introduce the school’s vision, build relationships, and invite more people into the work.

Every contribution helps build a school rooted in this place and sustained by the community it serves. To get involved, email us at info@canoevalley.org.

“Passion for learning comes most powerfully from desire, and love, or a mission to accomplish something personally meaningful. This has proven true in my own life for sure, as competencies and knowledge grew organically from what I loved and could not live without, or from a task that attended a great need of someone else’s. That such a pathway is being acknowledged and built into the fabric of Canoe Valley School through mentorship and creative planning for students’ individual interests, as well as community projects with student input, is a very inspiring and well-overdue option for our community.”

Heidi, Community Member
